verdict.rationale: Reducto's Parse endpoint explicitly outputs structured JSON with text, tables, figures, layout, and formatting (reducto-docs-1), and Split can identify page-level sections via natural language (reducto-docs-3/20), suggesting hierarchy/reading-order preservation is a design goal. However, no docs explicitly discuss heading-level structure or reading-order guarantees, and community reports note struggles on long (300+ page) documents needing workarounds like Deep Extract or switching to other models (reducto-comm-7, reducto-comm-8), which undercuts confidence in consistent structural fidelity at scale. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of heading/section hierarchy preservation, reading-order guarantees, and independent benchmarks confirming structural accuracy on long/complex documents.
